moat_source: CUDA software ecosystem, NVLink/networking fabric lock-in, and annual platform cadence; evidence: ~75% gross margin at $80B+ quarterly scale and $49B quarterly FCF - pricing power of this magnitude at this scale is the strongest moat evidence that exists

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% of the gap closed by year 3. Returns exclude the ~50%-of-FCF capital return stream, which adds roughly 2% annually - stated returns are conservative.

sensitivity_key_driver: hyperscaler capex trajectory FY2028-2029 (revenue growth path)
primary_model_risk: Capex cycle shape: base case assumes growth decelerates smoothly (35% to 8%) rather than a digestion year. AI infrastructure spending has never gone through a downcycle at this scale; if FY2028 capex flattens, bear-case FCF stagnation ($98 IV) becomes central, and the market would re-rate the multiple before the FCF actually printed.
expectations_gap_key_variable: growth duration: at 29.8x trailing (vs 44x its own 12-month average) the market prices meaningful deceleration; our base case is only modestly more constructive - the +14.6% margin of safety is real but not table-pounding
top_5_bull_arguments: $49B of quarterly free cash flow is not a story, it is arithmetic: ~24x annualized FCF for a company guiding +85% y/y growth
Multiple already compressed (29.8x vs 44x average) while earnings doubled - the derating happened without the earnings miss
Networking (+263% y/y) is compounding into a second wide-moat franchise inside the company
China DC revenue at zero in guidance = a free call option on any policy thaw
~50% of FCF returned to shareholders adds a ~2%/yr return floor the DCF ignores
top_5_bear_arguments: Revenue concentration in a handful of hyperscalers whose boards are all asking when AI capex pays back
Custom ASIC substitution grinds share away at exactly the horizon (yr 3-5) where terminal value lives
AI capex has never had a downcycle at this scale - the bear case is untested territory and the stock's beta (2.22) says the market knows it
Expected 5-yr return (+1.6% ex-buybacks) is thin for the risk taken; most of the value is already recognized
Geopolitical tail risks (Taiwan supply chain, export escalation) are unhedgeable and non-diversifiable at this position size in indices
thesis_breakers: First y/y decline in Data Center revenue
Gross margin below 70% for two consecutive quarters
A top-2 hyperscaler publicly shifting majority AI compute to internal silicon
FCF conversion falling below 40% of revenue
position_size_recommendation: 2-3%; the only name on this watchlist trading below expected intrinsic value, though the margin (14.6%) rewards patience for a wider entry on capex-cycle scares
notes_on_nulls: ROIC/ROE/ROA null: not captured as sourced ratios in pass1/claude_pass1; given 75% gross margins and $49B quarterly FCF on modest capital, ROIC is self-evidently extreme but stating a number without a source would violate the ground-truth constraint. Revenue, FCF, and guidance inputs are all reported (press releases/8-K) - the strongest data foundation on this watchlist; confidence_level medium only because the 5-year capex-cycle path is genuinely unknowable.
historical_context: Directional context only - low confidence. Verified datapoints: trailing P/E 29.84 vs 44.35 twelve-month average (public.com via pass1), stock roughly flat for 2026 (Yahoo Finance coverage), -1.35% past week. No verified 5-year multiple range beyond this captured.
